lesson_scope: Solving nested complex polynomial equations, determining parameter conditions for purely imaginary roots, equal modulus roots on circles, argument constraints, powers of roots on circles, and geometric properties of root polygons in the Argand plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Parameter value for purely imaginary root in cubic.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = \mathrm{i}y$ and equate imaginary part to zero:
$$-y^3 + 9y = 0 \implies y(9 - y^2) = 0 \implies y^2 = 9$$

Equate real part to zero:
$$-2y^2 + k = 0 \implies k = 2(9) = 18$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $z = \mathrm{i}y$ and equates imaginary part to zero to find $y^2 = 9$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Modulus condition on quadratic roots.

hints: By Vieta's formulas, product of roots is $k = 9$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply product of roots:
$$z_1 z_2 = z_1 \bar{z}_1 = |z_1|^2 = 3^2 = 9$$

Determine $k$:
$$k = z_1 z_2 = 9$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $|z|^2 = k$ using product of conjugate roots.

walkthrough.text:
Rearrange and take square roots:
$$(z - 2)^2 = -9 \implies z - 2 = \pm 3\mathrm{i}$$

Solve for $z$:
$$z = 2 \pm 3\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Parameter condition for root with specified argument.

walkthrough.text:
Find modulus of roots:
$$r^2 = 18 \implies r = 3\sqrt{2}$$

Calculate $p$ using sum of roots:
$$p = 2r\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 2(3\sqrt{2})\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 6$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Solving equation quadratic in z^3.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise in $z^3$:
$$(z^3 - 8)(z^3 + 1) = 0 \implies z^3 = 8 \text{ or } z^3 = -1$$

Find real roots:
$$z = \sqrt[3]{8} = 2, \quad z = \sqrt[3]{-1} = -1$$

Take square root of both sides:
$$z^2 + 5 = \pm 4 \implies z^2 = -1 \text{ or } z^2 = -9$$

Solve for $z$:
$$z = \pm\mathrm{i}, \quad z = \pm 3\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Cubic parameter for purely imaginary root and factorisation.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = \mathrm{i}y$ and equate imaginary part:
$$-y^3 + 4y = 0 \implies y(4 - y^2) = 0 \implies y = 2 \quad (y > 0)$$

Equate real part:
$$-3y^2 + k = 0 \implies k = 3(4) = 12$$

State all three roots:
$$z = -3, \quad z = 2\mathrm{i}, \quad z = -2\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Quartic with parameter expansion and root distance.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Determining quartic coefficients from quadratic factors.

walkthrough.text:
Form quadratic factors:
$$(z - (1 + 3\mathrm{i}))(z - (1 - 3\mathrm{i})) = z^2 - 2z + 10$$
$$P(z) = (z^2 - 2z + 10)(z^2 - 2z + c) \implies 10c = 50 \implies c = 5$$

Expand and equate coefficients:
$$(z^2 - 2z + 10)(z^2 - 2z + 5) = z^4 - 4z^3 + 19z^2 - 30z + 50$$
$$a = 19, \quad b = -30$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds $c = 5$ from constant term $10c = 50$ and expands.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding roots and distance between them.

walkthrough.text:
Solve second factor $z^2 - 2z + 5 = 0$:
$$z = 1 \pm 2\mathrm{i} \implies \text{Four roots: } 1 \pm 3\mathrm{i}, \quad 1 \pm 2\mathrm{i}$$

Calculate distance:
$$|(1 + 3\mathrm{i}) - (1 + 2\mathrm{i})| = |\mathrm{i}| = 1$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves second quadratic factor to get $1 \pm 2\mathrm{i}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Nested quartic root extraction and square geometry.

walkthrough.text:
Take square root:
$$(z - 1)^2 = \pm 2\mathrm{i}$$

Solve for $z$:
$$z - 1 = \pm(1 + \mathrm{i}) \implies z = 2 + \mathrm{i}, \; -\mathrm{i}$$
$$z - 1 = \pm(1 - \mathrm{i}) \implies z = 2 - \mathrm{i}, \; \mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Four roots: } 2 + \mathrm{i}, \quad 2 - \mathrm{i}, \quad \mathrm{i}, \quad -\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Takes square roots of $\pm 2\mathrm{i}$ to obtain $z - 1 = \pm(1 + \mathrm{i})$ and $z - 1 = \pm(1 - \mathrm{i})$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quadrilateral is square and finding area.

hints: All side lengths are $2$ and adjacent sides are perpendicular.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate side lengths and verify square:
$$\text{Vertices: } (2, 1), (0, 1), (0, -1), (2, -1)$$
$$\text{Side lengths: } |(2, 1) - (0, 1)| = 2, \quad |(0, 1) - (0, -1)| = 2, \dots$$
$$\text{All sides have length } 2 \text{ and are parallel to coordinate axes, so it is a square.}$$

Calculate area:
$$\text{Area} = 2^2 = 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explains adjacent sides are perpendicular, proving square.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Cubic parameter for roots on circle and triangle geometry.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding real root and parameter from modulus constraint.

hints: Product of all three roots is $5z_3 = 15 \implies z_3 = 3$.
Sum of roots is $z_1 + z_2 + 3 = 3 \implies z_1 + z_2 = 0 \implies k = 5$.

walkthrough.text:
Find real root using product of roots:
$$|z_1|^2 z_3 = 15 \implies 5z_3 = 15 \implies z_3 = 3$$

Find $k$ using sum of roots:
$$z_1 + z_2 + 3 = 3 \implies z_1 + z_2 = 0 \implies \text{Quadratic factor is } z^2 + 5$$
$$P(z) = (z - 3)(z^2 + 5) = z^3 - 3z^2 + 5z - 15 \implies k = 5$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses product of roots $5z_3 = 15$ to find real root $z_3 = 3$.
Uses sum of roots to get quadratic factor $z^2 + 5$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding perimeter and area of root triangle.

walkthrough.text:
State complex roots and side lengths:
$$\text{Roots: } A(3, 0), \; B(0, \sqrt{5}), \; C(0, -\sqrt{5})$$
$$AB = AC = \sqrt{3^2 + (\sqrt{5})^2} = \sqrt{14}, \quad BC = 2\sqrt{5}$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2\sqrt{14} + 2\sqrt{5}$$

Calculate area:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{5})(3) = 3\sqrt{5}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Sixth-degree polynomial, circle locus, and root powers.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise in $u = z^2$:
$$u^2(u - 2) + 4(u - 2) = (u - 2)(u^2 + 4) = 0$$
$$u = 2, \quad u = 2\mathrm{i}, \quad u = -2\mathrm{i}$$

Find all six roots:
$$z^2 = 2 \implies z = \pm\sqrt{2}$$
$$z^2 = 2\mathrm{i} \implies z = \pm(1 + \mathrm{i})$$
$$z^2 = -2\mathrm{i} \implies z = \pm(1 - \mathrm{i})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Takes square roots of $\pm 2\mathrm{i}$ to obtain $\pm(1 + \mathrm{i})$ and $\pm(1 - \mathrm{i})$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving roots lie on circle and calculating power.

walkthrough.text:
Verify modulus of all roots:
$$|\pm\sqrt{2}| = \sqrt{2}, \quad |\pm 1 \pm \mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$$
$$\text{All six roots lie on the circle } |z| = \sqrt{2}, \text{ with radius } R = \sqrt{2}.$$

Calculate eighth power for non-real roots:
$$z = \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta} \implies z^8 = (\sqrt{2})^8 \mathrm{e}^{8\mathrm{i}\theta} = 16\mathrm{e}^{2k\pi\mathrm{i}} = 16$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates modulus of all six roots to show $|z| = \sqrt{2}$.
Expresses non-real roots in polar form.
Evaluates $z^8 = 16$ for all four non-real roots.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Cubic with roots forming equilateral triangle.

hints: Arguments of equally spaced roots are $0, \frac{2\pi}{3}, -\frac{2\pi}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine arguments of equally spaced roots:
$$\theta_1 = 0, \quad \theta_2 = \frac{2\pi}{3}, \quad \theta_3 = -\frac{2\pi}{3}$$

Convert $z_2$ to Cartesian form:
$$z_2 = 2\left(\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} + \mathrm{i}\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = -1 + \mathrm{i}\sqrt{3} \implies u = -1, \quad v = \sqrt{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets arguments of equally spaced roots.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding coefficients and area of equilateral triangle.

walkthrough.text:
Compute parameters $p$ and $q$:
$$p = z_1 + z_2 + z_3 = 2 - 1 + \mathrm{i}\sqrt{3} - 1 - \mathrm{i}\sqrt{3} = 0$$
$$q = z_1 z_2 + z_1 z_3 + z_2 z_3 = 2(-2) + (1 + 3) = -4 + 4 = 0$$

Calculate area of equilateral triangle:
$$s = |2 - (-1 + \mathrm{i}\sqrt{3})| = |3 - \mathrm{i}\sqrt{3}| = 2\sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(2\sqrt{3})^2 = 3\sqrt{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Quartic parameter, root finding, and trapezium geometry.

walkthrough.text:
Form first quadratic factor:
$$(z - (1 + 2\mathrm{i}))(z - (1 - 2\mathrm{i})) = z^2 - 2z + 5$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding all four roots of quartic.

walkthrough.text:
State first conjugate pair:
$$z_1 = 1 + 2\mathrm{i}, \quad z_2 = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$$

Solve second factor $z^2 - 6z + 10 = 0$:
$$z = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 40}}{2} = 3 \pm \mathrm{i} \implies z_3 = 3 + \mathrm{i}, \quad z_4 = 3 - \mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Four roots: } 1 + 2\mathrm{i}, \quad 1 - 2\mathrm{i}, \quad 3 + \mathrm{i}, \quad 3 - \mathrm{i}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quadrilateral is isosceles trapezium and calculating area.

hints: $AD$ on $x = 1$, length $4$; $BC$ on $x = 3$, length $2$. Parallel because vertical.

walkthrough.text:
Prove quadrilateral is an isosceles trapezium:
$$AD = |2 - (-2)| = 4 \quad (\text{on } x = 1)$$
$$BC = |1 - (-1)| = 2 \quad (\text{on } x = 3)$$
$$AD \parallel BC \text{ since both are vertical.}$$
$$AB = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (1 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{5}, \quad DC = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (-1 - (-2))^2} = \sqrt{5}$$
$$\text{Since } AB = DC, \; ABCD \text{ is an isosceles trapezium.}$$

Calculate area:
$$\text{Height } h = 3 - 1 = 2$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(4 + 2)(2) = 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Shows $AD \parallel BC$ with lengths $4$ and $2$, and $AB = DC = \sqrt{5}$.
